session.question: How did broiler chicks in Iraq compare in maternal derived antibodies against Newcastle disease vaccination, and which strain performed better in the study?
session.answer: In 1-day-old imported broiler chicks from Nineveh/Mosul governorate, Iraq, maternal derived antibodies against Newcastle disease vaccination were high and relatively uniform in both evaluated strains, based on indirect ELISA testing of 707 samples from Ross 308 and Cobb 500 flocks. Cobb 500 chicks showed a stronger serological profile, with 100% positivity compared with 97.78% in Ross 308, a higher mean maternal antibody titer (9,871.47 vs 8,647.76), a lower coefficient of variation (12.41% vs 15.18%), and a higher vaccination index (966.59 vs 821.60). These findings indicate that both strains had protective maternal titers, but Cobb 500 performed better overall and was concluded to have higher protective titers than Ross 308. (ezzulddin2022theabilityto chunk 1)

pqac-a57d0d29: The study compared maternal derived antibodies against Newcastle disease vaccination in 1-day-old imported broiler chicks in Nineveh/Mosul governorate, Iraq. It sampled 707 chicks from 28 Ross 308 flocks (451 samples) and 17 Cobb 500 flocks (256 samples) using indirect ELISA. Results showed both strains had high and fairly uniform maternal antibody titers, but Cobb 500 chicks performed better: 100% positivity versus 97.78% in Ross 308, higher mean titer (9,871.47 vs 8,647.76), lower CV (12.41% vs 15.18%), and a higher vaccination index (966.59 vs 821.60). The conclusion was that Cobb 500 had higher protective titers than Ross 308.
From Thamer Abdulazeez Ezzulddin, Dhyaa Mohammad Taher Jwher, and Akeel Mohammad Shareef. The ability to resist newcastle disease through inherited immunity in different strains of broilers in nineveh governorate. Open Veterinary Journal, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.5455/ovj.2022.v12.i6.20, doi:10.5455/ovj.2022.v12.i6.20.

pqac-ea38ab23: The study compared maternal derived antibodies against Newcastle disease vaccination in 1-day-old imported broiler chicks from two strains in Nineveh/Mosul governorate: Cobb 500 and Ross 308. A total of 707 blood samples were tested using an indirect ELISA. Results showed Cobb 500 performed better than Ross 308: 100% positivity vs 97.78%, higher mean maternal antibody titer (9,871.47 vs 8,647.76), lower CV (12.41% vs 15.18%), and higher vaccination index (966.59 vs 821.60). The conclusion states both strains had high and uniform titers, but Cobb 500 produced chicks with higher protective titers than Ross 308.
From Thamer Abdulazeez Ezzulddin, Dhyaa Mohammad Taher Jwher, and Akeel Mohammad Shareef. pqac-c337aff9: The excerpt is about a 2017 study on maternal dietary zinc supplementation in broiler breeder hens, examining how zinc and maternal temperature affected chick embryo development, oxidative damage, and epigenetic regulation of antioxidant genes. It reports that zinc supplementation reduced embryonic mortality under heat stress and increased metallothionein IV expression through changes in DNA methylation and histone acetylation. This paper focuses on maternal diet, heat stress, and embryonic antioxidant protection in chickens, not on maternal-derived antibodies, Newcastle disease vaccination strains, Iraq broiler chicks, or performance comparisons of vaccination studies.
From Yongwen Zhu, Xiudong Liao, Lin Lu, Wenxiang Li, Liyang Zhang, Cheng Ji, Xi Lin, Hsiao-Ching Liu, Jack Odle, and Xugang Luo. Maternal dietary zinc supplementation enhances the epigenetic-activated antioxidant ability of chick embryos from maternal normal and high temperatures. Oncotarget, 2017.
